patches_submitted.subject: [RFC PATCH] btrfs: trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio()

version_history.subject: [RFC PATCH] btrfs: trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio()

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch proposes a new approach to trigger the COW (Copy-On-Write) fixup in Btrfs via the dirty_folio() function, which is used to handle folios that have been improperly dirtied during writeback. The current implementation uses an asynchronous worker to catch and fix such cases, but this patch aims to simplify the process by leveraging the dirty_folio() function. This change addresses a long-standing issue where a dio read may skip dirtying a folio if it is already clean by the end of the I/O operation, leading to potential data corruption. The patch maintains three critical invariants to ensure that each block is written exactly once: any dirty block is covered by delalloc or an ordered extent, any dirty block submitted into an OE will be written back within that OE, and any dirty block already submitted into an OE will not be resubmitted. This change aims to demonstrate a more complex solution to the problem and highlight the issues it must address.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that the patch does not properly handle the case where a dio read is in progress and btrfs finishes writing back the folio, causing the dio to re-dirty the folio unnecessarily. They requested that the dirty_folio() call be moved after the folio is unlocked.

The reviewer is concerned that the patch's complexity and size are overwhelming due to its rapid development by an LLM, which may lead to issues in review and maintenance.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that the call to trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio() is very frequent and redundant, suggesting that it can be merged into btrfs_folio*_set_dirty(), which ensures proper dirtying and cancellation of the fixup.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested simplifying the dirty_folio() check by only verifying if the fixup bit is not set, as this indicates that the folio has gone through regular write preparation and should have EXTENT_DELALLOC.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested replacing the use of btrfs_is_subpage() and related functions from subpage.c with a custom helper function, btrfs_folio_test_fixup(), to improve code readability.

The reviewer noted that if a folio has already been dirtied properly, calling ->dirty_folio() may trigger a false alert because there might be no ordered extent (OE) created yet for the folio, violating one of the critical invariants.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested simplifying the code by skipping ordered extent (OE) lookup and letting the final submission path handle it, citing a recent patch that achieves similar functionality at submission time.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo expressed concern about the variable naming in the patch, stating that it appears to be generated by a Large Language Model (LLM) and may require additional explanation for non-native speakers.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo questioned whether triggering cow fixup via dirty_folio() is necessary because the folio has not yet been dirtied, and expressed uncertainty about the need for this patch.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested using btrfs_folio_clear_fixup() instead of the proposed fix to trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio(), indicating that their preferred approach is more helpful.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo expressed frustration with the LLM's comments and suggested deleting them by default, implying that they are unnecessary or unhelpful.

The reviewer, Qu Wenruo, pointed out that the patch can lead to over-reservation of space for already properly dirtied ranges, making it impossible to release reserved space without clearing qgroup flags. This issue is difficult to expose through tests because dirty folios are hard to trigger.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested using a proper btrfs_folio_clear_fixup() function to handle the loop, passing in the folio range instead of relying on dirty_folio().

Reviewer Qu Wenruo pointed out that the patch's approach to handling dirty folios via dirty_folio() is unnecessary, as regular btrfs_folio_clear_dirty() can handle all these cases and there's no need for a special subpage branch.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo questioned the necessity of using dirty_folio() when folio_test_dirty() would be sufficient, specifically pointing out that the subpage part does not have this check.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that calling folio_mark_dirty() would lead to a recursive call to ->dirty_folio(), and instead implemented a local version of filemap_mark_dirty() to set the fixup bits.

The reviewer noted that the patch may not fully address the COW fixup issue, suggesting that additional checks are needed to ensure that the last fixup bit is cleared and the folio fixup flag is reset.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested that the btrfs_page_ops implementation should handle all fixup helpers, rather than relying on a separate dirty_folio() function.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that since btrfs_folio_set_dirty() does not call folio_mark_dirty(), the fixup bit is not actually being set, and suggested removing the dirty_folio() call to skip setting the fixup bit.
review_comments.raw_body:
在 2026/7/25 15:54, Boris Burkov 写道:
[...]>

---

Without LLM it's very hard to come up with such huge change in such a 
short time, especially considering this fix is a little urgent due to 
both large folio and removal of cow fixup are in the same release.

So I'm totally fine with the involvement of LLM, just we will spend 
quite some time reworking/removing a lot of comments/commit message.

Not because they are not not grammarly sound (unlike my replies), but a 
lot of time they are too lengthy but brings not too much value compared 
to the number of lines.

But still, very impressed to see a working RFC this soon.

---

This call is very frequent, and to be honest, it's redundant.

We can merge the cancel into btrfs_folio*_set_dirty(), as the 
btrfs_folio_*set_dirty() is the "proper dirty" entrance, so we know if 
we're going through that interface, we are ensured to cancel the fixup.

---

Can we simplify the check to just check if the fixup bit is not set?

To me, without fixup bit it means it went through the regular write 
preparation, thus should have EXTENT_DELALLOC.
And checking a bit is way faster than check an extent range.

---

Again, we prefer not to use btrfs_is_subpage() and btrfs_subpage_*() out 
of subpage.c when possible.

So just some helper, like btrfs_folio_test_fixup() would make it more 
readable.

---

The block can be dirtied properly before, then ->dirty_folio() callback 
is triggered.

In that case, we may have not run delalloc for the folio, thus there may 
be no OE created yet.

It looks like the assumption is not correct to me, and may cause false 
alerts.

But on the other hand, it's already very hard to hit a case where we 
have some proper dirty blocks, and ->dirty_folio() is called.
E.g. for the direct IO case, ->dirty_folio() is only called when the 
folio is clean.

Thus this false alerts case is not easy to test.

---

Doing this is a little overkilled.

As the recent patch "btrfs: use ordered extent to grab the logical 
address for submission" will do it at submission time, with better 
cached OE usage.

I'd prefer skip the OE lookup completely, and let the final submission 
path to grab the OE (which can reuse bbio->ordered when possible).

---

The variable naming choice is definitely very LLM.

Non-native speaker like me may need to google the word first...

---

We haven't yet cleared any bit nor folio dirty in the first place.
So not sure if this is really needed, nor the comment.

---

Again, a btrfs_folio_clear_fixup() is more helpful.

[...]

---

Again, very LLM comments. That's why always delete all comments from LLM 
by default.

The older, removed comment is very simple for folio_ordered:

  * We use folio flag owner_2 to indicate there is an ordered extent with
  * unfinished IO.


[...]

---

You fall into the same pitfall I'm worried about, but unfortunately or 
fortunately, it's very hard to hit.

The problem here is, we can over-reserve, e.g. some range is already 
properly dirtied, thus they have already space reserved.

And you can not release the reserved space for them, because release 
will also clear the qgroup reserved extent flag.

This is the biggest problem that I have no way to fix.
As there is no way to ensure the space we reserved is really needed 
before holding the folio lock.


But since it's really hard to get a dirty folio to be called with 
->dirty_folio(), thus it may not be exposed through tests.

---

Again, a proper btrfs_folio_clear_fixup() and pass the folio range into 
it should handle the loop.

---

Again, the regular btrfs_folio_clear_dirty() is going to handle all 
these, and no need for a special subpage branch.

---

Again, the same question why the folio_test_dirty() check is not enough.

The subpage part has no such check.

---

My solution in my initial patchset is to not call folio_mark_dirty() as 
it will call back to the ->dirty_folio() call back.

So I implemented an local version which call back to 
filemap_mark_dirty(), other than ->dirty_folio() which sets the fixup bits.

---

Shouldn't we also check if we have cleared the last fixup bit and clear 
the folio fixup flag?
[...]

---

Why not let IMPLEMNT_BTRFS_PAGE_OPS() to implement all the fixup helpers?

[...]

---

As I mentioned, this is only for dirty_folio() to skip setting fixup bit.

We can get rid of it, if the btrfs_folio_set_dirty() helper doesn't go 
through folio_mark_dirty().

Thanks,
Qu

review_comments.author: Boris Burkov (author)
review_comments.summary:
Author acknowledged that some invariants were not properly trimmed from the LLM-generated code and agreed to rework them.

Author acknowledged that the delalloc lookup is essential for distinguishing between re-dirtying and true fixups, but is considering simplifying the code by removing the possibility of re-dirtying in typical cases.

Author acknowledged that the code to check if ordered extent is present is unnecessary and agreed to simplify the logic by removing or hiding it, depending on the configuration.

The author acknowledged a minor issue with technical terminology and promised to correct it.

Author acknowledged a concern about the complexity of the proposed fixup worker and its potential for 'word salad' code, but did not indicate plans to revise or restructure the patch.

Author acknowledged a potential issue where aops->dirty_folio() is called without locking the folio, but believes the current implementation's strategy of reserving the whole range and then freeing parts that don't get 'funded' should handle cancellations correctly. However, they acknowledge it's an ugly solution and consider an alternative approach with locking to be appealing but potentially flawed due to a TOCTOU race.

Author acknowledges that avoiding the 'bfs->reserving_dirty' approach is a good idea and seems open to revising their patch, but doesn't explicitly state they will make changes.

Author agrees that using dirty_folio() is an improvement, acknowledges current implementation as a 'stupid way' that introduces unnecessary risk, but does not indicate plans to revise the patch.
sentiment_signals: did not indicate plans to revise
review_comments.raw_body:
100% agreed, I tried to trim them down and rewrite them in human but
missed a bunch in the rush.

---

the delalloc lookup is essential for bs == folio_size, to tell apart
the case where you are submitting a folio that got redirtied behind you
(don't skip) and the case where it is a true fixup.

Thinking about it more, though, that re-dirty shouldn't really be
possible at least in typical cases, so maybe I can figure out how to
remove this.

I think for subpage it probably doesn't matter, because those should not
have fixup in their bitmaps.

---

Agreed. This is vestigial from a long period where ordered was really
important before I tightened the logic and left it as an assertion, but
that is a big overkill for not DEBUG at least. I'll either remove it or
hide it behind CONFIG_BTRFS_DEBUG.

---

Yes, I hate when they do that. This one was just natural enough to me
that I let it go, but it is totally pointless jargon. I'll fix it.

---

yup, haha missed this one. You would have loved the ones that got
deleted :D

it was like scrolls full of word salad at every if(...)

---

I think this approach here seems correct to me, except for maybe a
really mean case which calls aops->dirty_folio() without locking the folio
(not the case for dio read at least).

Won't any real reservation will cancel the fixup bits under the lock, so
the way this implementation tries to handle it is to reserve the whole
range then free the parts that don't end up getting in the "funded"
bitmap (also a bad LLM name...). This is checking the fixup bitmap under
the lock, so should see correct cancellations. Do you see an obvious
problem with that strategy, besides that it is kind of ugly and annoying
to handle the 'out:' path. Which feels similarly painful to a lot of our
other delalloc/qgroup_rsv unwinding logic with data_reserveds on OE error
or whatnot.

I think the clearer option of "take the lock, observe the real set,
release, then reserve, then take the lock and do all the work" sounds
appealing but almost certainly fails to some simple TOCTOU race.

---

You mean to avoid the ugly bfs->reserving_dirty thing?
That does sound appealing...

---

yes, that seems like an obvious improvement. I think we get away with it
in a super stupid way that writepage_fixup will walk the bitmap and see
all clear and clear it there. Complete waste and adds risk for no
reason.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested using folio->private to indicate a folio is properly dirtied, similar to how the subpage dirty bit works in the bs == folio size case.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that the patch requires a local function btrfs_folio_mark_dirty_prepared() to copy folio_mark_dirty(), but call filemap_dirty_folio() instead of using aops->dirty_folio, and expressed uncertainty about whether MM will be happy with this change.
review_comments.raw_body:
In that case, I'd prefer to use folio->private to have one extra bit, to 
indicate the folio is properly dirtied.

E.g. this commit in my unfinished branch:
https://github.com/adam900710/linux/commit/9a02921d348574573f1a6dbc50e54f993011e311

Which acts like the subpage dirty bit for bs == folio size case.

---

Yep. However the ugly part is, we will need a local 
"btrfs_folio_mark_dirty_prepared()", which copies "folio_mark_dirty()", 
except call filemap_dirty_folio() instead of using aops->dirty_folio.

Not sure if MM will be happy about that.

Thanks,
Qu

patches_reviewed.subject: Re: [RFC PATCH] btrfs: trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio()
patches_reviewed.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Btrfs file system to trigger cow (copy-on-write) fixup via dirty_folio(). The change aims to improve handling of delalloc lookup and reservation in the presence of subpage folios, which are not expected to have fixup bits. It also removes vestigial code related to ordered operations and reworks the implementation to handle potential TOCTOU (time-of-check-to-time-of-use) races. The patch introduces a new approach to reserve the whole range and then free parts that don't end up in the 'funded' bitmap, which is considered an improvement over the previous implementation.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested using folio->private to add an extra bit indicating whether a folio is properly dirtied, similar to the subpage dirty bit for bs == folio size case.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo pointed out the need for a local function, btrfs_folio_mark_dirty_prepared(), which would copy folio_mark_dirty() but call filemap_dirty_folio() instead of aops->dirty_folio(). They expressed uncertainty about whether MM will be happy with this change.
review_comments.raw_body:
In that case, I'd prefer to use folio->private to have one extra bit, to 
indicate the folio is properly dirtied.

E.g. this commit in my unfinished branch:
https://github.com/adam900710/linux/commit/9a02921d348574573f1a6dbc50e54f993011e311

Which acts like the subpage dirty bit for bs == folio size case.

---

"btrfs_folio_mark_dirty_prepared()", which copies "folio_mark_dirty()", 
except call filemap_dirty_folio() instead of using aops->dirty_folio.

Not sure if MM will be happy about that.

Thanks,
Qu
